matters.heading: Summary of preliminary competition concerns
matters.excerpt: In Canberra, which does not have petrol price cycles, the Acquisition would remove a direct competitor to Ampol and lead to Ampol becoming the largest fuel retailer in that metropolitan market. The ACCC’s preliminary assessment is that the Acquisition would have the effect, or likely effect, of substantially lessening competition in the retail supply of fuel in Canberra from coordinated effects becoming more likely, more complete and/or more sustainable across the remaining retailers. matters.heading: Summary of preliminary competition concerns

matters.heading: Summary of preliminary competition assessment
matters.excerpt: The limitations with GUPPIs and IPRs are well recognised. First, it is often challenging to obtain suitable inputs to perform the calculations. Secondly, the estimates are static measures, not dynamic. In this respect, Dr Jill Walker has noted that: Neither UPPs nor IPRs take account of the likely competitive response from actual and potential rivals.  For this reason, they cannot provide a complete analysis as to the likelihood of competitive harm arising from a merger.  Rather they provide an alternative and more focussed way of filtering mergers for potential unilateral effects compared to calculating market shares.

matters.heading: Background
matters.excerpt: In addition, in the major cities such as Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth, petrol prices move up and down in regular patterns. These patterns are known as petrol price cycles. Petrol price cycles are not driven by movements in wholesale prices or underlying costs and not all retailers participate in price cycles. Price cycles do not occur for retail diesel and automotive LPG prices.

matters.heading: Background
matters.excerpt: Typically in a price cycle, prices at individual retail sites increase sharply, then decrease more gradually over a longer period before the process repeats. Not all retail sites change prices at the same time, meaning average metropolitan-wide prices can take time to increase (and decrease).

matters.heading: Background
matters.excerpt: The ACCC has also observed differences in petrol price cycle patterns in Australia’s largest cities over time. For example, in the year to September 2025, cycles in Sydney were around 5 and a half weeks in duration while in Melbourne they were around 6 and a half weeks and in Brisbane around 7 weeks. Previously, in 2018, the ACCC observed that cycles in the same three cities were about a month long.

matters.heading: Background
matters.excerpt: Smaller cities such as Canberra, Hobart and Darwin and most regional areas do not have petrol price cycles.

matters.heading: Overlap and relevant areas of competition
matters.excerpt: In addition to local market competition, evidence before the ACCC indicates that it is also appropriate to consider the competitive effect of the Acquisition on metropolitan areas in which Ampol and EG Australia are among the largest fuel retail networks. In cities with petrol price cycles, the existence of those price cycles appears to be evidence of, or at least consistent with, retailers monitoring and responding to the pricing behaviour of competitors across a metropolitan area and not just locally.

matters.heading: Market definition
matters.excerpt: The Parties submit that an appropriate product dimension for the Acquisition is personal lines general insurance, which includes (among other products) motor vehicle insurance and home and contents insurance. In support of this, IAG identified certain supply side complementarities that exist between different personal lines general insurance products, such as branding and distribution efficiencies. Further, IAG notes that it is generally easier for existing suppliers of personal lines insurance products to expand their offering to include other personal lines insurance products than it is to achieve completely new entry.

matters.heading: Market definition
matters.excerpt: while insurers can expand from one type of insurance to another, the time and investment required in achieving this means this is better understood as new entry, rather than supply-side substitution. Home and contents insurance is significantly more capital intensive than motor vehicle insurance. It involves more complex risk assessment, which requires different and more extensive data to set premiums. As such, rivals in the supply of motor vehicle insurance that are seeking to move into also supplying home and contents insurance would face substantial challenges and costs.

matters.heading: Summary of preliminary competition assessment
matters.excerpt: There have been few genuine new entrants to the supply of motor vehicle insurance in Australia in recent years, with the most recent successful new entry being Youi in 2008. The ACCC has not been able to identify any examples of likely new entrants able to provide a sufficient constraint on IAG in a timely manner.

matters.heading: Summary of preliminary competition assessment
matters.excerpt: The ACCC considers barriers to entry into the supply of home and contents insurance are higher than for motor vehicle insurance. As noted in Section 3, home and contents insurance is significantly more capital intensive than motor vehicle insurance. It also involves more complex risk assessment, which requires different and more extensive data to set premiums. As such, rivals seeking to expand from supplying motor vehicle insurance to home and contents insurance would incur substantial challenges and costs.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The various ways and extent to which competition takes place in the supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia (including price, coverage and other terms of the insurance product offering, customer service, claims handling and renewals).

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The competitive constraint from rival insurers on IAG post-Acquisition in Western Australia.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The impact of the use of different brands (both underwriter and third-party brands) on competition for consumers.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: How regulatory costs, claims cost volatility, reinsurance costs and geographic diversity impact RACI’s ability to supply home and contents insurance.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The extent to which RACI’s motor insurance portfolio could mitigate against loss events in RACI’s home and contents insurance portfolio.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The various ways and extent to which competition takes place in the supply motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia (including price, coverage and other terms of the insurance product offering, service quality, claims handling and renewals).

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The competitive constraint from rival insurers on IAG post-Acquisition in Western Australia.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The impact of the use of different brands (both underwriter and third-party brands) on competition for consumers.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: How regulatory costs, claims cost volatility, reinsurance costs and geographic diversity impact RACI’s ability to supply motor vehicle insurance. Vertical effects

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: Whether there are regions in Western Australia where smash repair services are limited or capacity constrained.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The degree to which contractual arrangements with smash repairers provide for exclusivity or priority access.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
matters.excerpt: The extent to which smash repairers in practice prioritise work from larger insurers.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the acquisition of motor vehicle smash repair services
matters.excerpt: Whether smash repairers differ by size, quality, and efficiency in Western Australia and/or certain regions in Western Australia.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the acquisition of motor vehicle smash repair services
matters.excerpt: The extent to which repair-cost models of insurers influence the prices paid to smash repairers.

matters.heading: Competitive effects in the acquisition of motor vehicle smash repair services
matters.excerpt: The effect of lower repair prices on exit, entry, and investment decisions of smash repairers in Western Australia and/or certain regions in Western Australia.

matters.heading: Relevant areas of competition
matters.excerpt: The extent to which there are discrete product markets for calibration services within certain testing domains.

matters.heading: Relevant areas of competition
matters.excerpt: The extent to which there are narrower geographic markets within Australia for calibration services in certain testing domains, for example where equipment cannot be transported across significant distances.

matters.heading: Relevant areas of competition
matters.excerpt: Whether certain types of calibration tests need to be performed at a customer’s site, for example because the bulk or sensitivity of the equipment being calibrated means it cannot be transported to the calibration service provider’s laboratory for testing.

matters.heading: Competition effects in the supply of calibration services to customers that require multiple calibration services across a range of testing domains
matters.excerpt: The extent to which customers rely on a calibration service supplier to supply a broad range of calibration services across multiple testing domains, and the extent to which customers can multi-source from various suppliers.
